survey: A western saddle lies on a wooden fence rail, seen from the near side. The horn is a short post with a round cap on the pommel at the left. The seat dips into a suede-padded hollow and rises to the cantle at the right. One rectangular skirt hangs on the near side, and the far skirt shows behind it at the right. The rail runs left to right under the seat, through the gullet between the two skirts, so the saddle rests on it the way a real saddle rests on a rail. A near-side stirrup leather comes out under the seat roll, runs down over the skirt and ends in a metal buckle. That leather loops around the top bar of a wooden stirrup. The far stirrup hangs behind and to the right of the near one, and only its top shows below the bottom edge of the near skirt. There is no cinch or latigo, which is an acceptable simplification.

errors.where: Far (back) stirrup, under the bottom edge of the near skirt at center-right
errors.what: The far stirrup comes out from under the near skirt on a very short stub, with no stirrup leather running down the far side of the saddle. It looks as if it hangs from the underside of the near skirt, in the space between the skirts where the rail sits, not from the far side of the tree. It also sits too close beside the near stirrup for a saddle this wide on a thick rail.

errors.where: Left end of the seat and pommel where they meet the rail
errors.what: The rail's top edge on the left sits level with or slightly above the underside of the seat roll. The rail seems to pass into the saddle body instead of the gullet sitting on top of it.

fix: Hang the far stirrup from its own leather on the far side of the saddle, outside the far skirt, so it shows only partly behind the rail and the far skirt. Have the saddle's gullet clearly straddle the top of the fence rail, with the seat sitting above the rail and the skirts draping down both sides.
